title: Everything from a table
prompt: Return every column and every row of the ProductCategory table.
hint: SELECT * returns all columns. Tables live in the SalesLT schema (database SalesLT on MySQL).

answer.default: SELECT * FROM SalesLT.ProductCategory;

title: Pick columns
prompt: List the ProductID, Name, ProductNumber and ListPrice of every product.

answer.default:
SELECT ProductID, Name, ProductNumber, ListPrice
FROM SalesLT.Product;

title: Computed column
prompt: List each product's Name, ListPrice, StandardCost and the margin (ListPrice minus StandardCost) as a column named Margin.
hint: Use an expression in the SELECT list and give it an alias with AS.

answer.default:
SELECT Name, ListPrice, StandardCost, ListPrice - StandardCost AS Margin
FROM SalesLT.Product;

title: DISTINCT values
prompt: List each distinct Color used by products, once each (NULL counts as one value).

answer.default:
SELECT DISTINCT Color
FROM SalesLT.Product;

title: Concatenate strings
prompt: Return CustomerID and the customer's full name as 'FirstName LastName' (one space between) in a column named FullName.
hint: CONCAT() works on all three. SQL Server also has +, Postgres has ||.

answer.default:
SELECT CustomerID, CONCAT(FirstName, ' ', LastName) AS FullName
FROM SalesLT.Customer;
answer.sqlserver:
SELECT CustomerID, FirstName + ' ' + LastName AS FullName
FROM SalesLT.Customer;
answer.postgres:
SELECT CustomerID, FirstName || ' ' || LastName AS FullName
FROM SalesLT.Customer;

title: Equality filter
prompt: Return ProductID, Name and ListPrice of all products whose Color is 'Red'.

title: AND conditions
prompt: Return ProductID, Name and ListPrice of black products with a ListPrice greater than 1000.

title: IN list
prompt: Return AddressID, City and StateProvince of addresses in California, Oregon or Washington.

title: BETWEEN
prompt: Return ProductID, Name and ListPrice of products priced from 100 to 500 inclusive.
hint: BETWEEN includes both ends.

title: IS NULL
prompt: Return ProductID and Name of products that have no Color.
hint: Color = NULL is never true. Use IS NULL.

title: IS NOT NULL
prompt: Return CustomerID, FirstName, LastName and Suffix of customers that have a Suffix.

title: LIKE: starts with
prompt: Return ProductID and Name of products whose Name starts with 'Mountain'.

title: Case-insensitive search
prompt: Return CustomerID and CompanyName of customers whose CompanyName contains 'bike' in any letter case (Bike, BIKE, bike...).
hint: SQL Server and MySQL collations here are case-insensitive, so LIKE is enough. Postgres LIKE is case-sensitive: use ILIKE or LOWER().

title: LIKE with _ wildcard
prompt: Return ProductID, Name and ProductNumber of products whose ProductNumber has 'R' as its 4th character.
hint: _ matches exactly one character, % matches any number.

title: Top 10 most expensive
prompt: Return Name and ListPrice of the 10 most expensive products, highest price first. Break ties by Name ascending.
hint: SQL Server: SELECT TOP n. MySQL and Postgres: LIMIT n at the end.

answer.default:
SELECT Name, ListPrice
FROM SalesLT.Product
ORDER BY ListPrice DESC, Name
LIMIT 10;

title: Sort by several columns
prompt: Return ProductID, Name, Color and ListPrice of all products sorted by Color ascending, then ListPrice descending, then ProductID ascending.
hint: Where NULLs sort differs by database: first on SQL Server and MySQL, last on Postgres.

title: Paging with OFFSET
prompt: Customers sorted by CustomerID, 10 per page. Return page 3 (rows 21 to 30): CustomerID and CompanyName.
hint: SQL Server: OFFSET n ROWS FETCH NEXT m ROWS ONLY (needs ORDER BY). Others: LIMIT m OFFSET n.

answer.sqlserver:
SELECT CustomerID, CompanyName
FROM SalesLT.Customer
ORDER BY CustomerID
OFFSET 20 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY;
answer.default:
SELECT CustomerID, CompanyName
FROM SalesLT.Customer
ORDER BY CustomerID
LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20;

title: Cheapest colored products
prompt: Return ProductID, Name, Color and ListPrice of the 5 cheapest products that have a Color. Order by ListPrice ascending, then ProductID.

answer.sqlserver:
SELECT TOP 5 ProductID, Name, Color, ListPrice
FROM SalesLT.Product
WHERE Color IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY ListPrice, ProductID;
answer.default:
SELECT ProductID, Name, Color, ListPrice
FROM SalesLT.Product
WHERE Color IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY ListPrice, ProductID
LIMIT 5;

title: COUNT rows
prompt: How many customers are there? Return a single number.

answer.default:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount
FROM SalesLT.Customer;

title: MIN / MAX / AVG
prompt: Return the lowest, highest and average ListPrice of all products (three columns, in that order).

answer.default:
SELECT MIN(ListPrice) AS MinPrice, MAX(ListPrice) AS MaxPrice, AVG(ListPrice) AS AvgPrice
FROM SalesLT.Product;

title: GROUP BY
prompt: Return each Color (including NULL) and how many products have it.

title: SUM per group
prompt: From SalesOrderDetail, return each ProductID and the total quantity sold (sum of OrderQty).

title: HAVING
prompt: Return Color and product count for colors that have more than 30 products.
hint: WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters groups after.

answer.default:
SELECT Color, COUNT(*) AS ProductCount
FROM SalesLT.Product
GROUP BY Color
HAVING COUNT(*) > 30;

title: COUNT DISTINCT
prompt: How many different cities appear in the Address table? Return a single number.

answer.default:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT City) AS Cities
FROM SalesLT.Address;

title: Group by two columns
prompt: Return CountryRegion, StateProvince and the number of addresses in each, sorted by CountryRegion then StateProvince.

answer.default:
SELECT CountryRegion, StateProvince, COUNT(*) AS Addresses
FROM SalesLT.Address
GROUP BY CountryRegion, StateProvince
ORDER BY CountryRegion, StateProvince;

title: INNER JOIN
prompt: Return each product's Name and the Name of its category (two columns: product name, category name).

title: Order lines with products
prompt: For order 71774, return each line's product Name, OrderQty and UnitPrice.

answer.default:
SELECT p.Name, d.OrderQty, d.UnitPrice
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail d
JOIN SalesLT.Product p ON p.ProductID = d.ProductID
WHERE d.SalesOrderID = 71774;

title: JOIN + GROUP BY
prompt: For every order return SalesOrderID, the customer's CompanyName, the number of order lines and the order's TotalDue.

answer.default:
SELECT h.SalesOrderID, c.CompanyName, COUNT(*) AS LineCount, h.TotalDue
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderHeader h
JOIN SalesLT.Customer c ON c.CustomerID = h.CustomerID
JOIN SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail d ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID
GROUP BY h.SalesOrderID, c.CompanyName, h.TotalDue;

title: LEFT JOIN: find missing rows
prompt: Return CustomerID, FirstName and LastName of customers who have never placed an order.
hint: LEFT JOIN keeps every customer. Customers without orders get NULLs in the order columns.

answer.default:
SELECT c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
FROM SalesLT.Customer c
LEFT JOIN SalesLT.SalesOrderHeader h ON h.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
WHERE h.SalesOrderID IS NULL;

title: Self join
prompt: Categories form a two-level tree (ParentProductCategoryID points to the same table). For every subcategory return its Name and its parent category's Name.
hint: Join ProductCategory to itself, using two different aliases.

title: Many-to-many join
prompt: Customers and addresses are linked through CustomerAddress. Return CompanyName, City and StateProvince for every customer's 'Main Office' address.

answer.default:
SELECT c.CompanyName, a.City, a.StateProvince
FROM SalesLT.Customer c
JOIN SalesLT.CustomerAddress ca ON ca.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
JOIN SalesLT.Address a ON a.AddressID = ca.AddressID
WHERE ca.AddressType = 'Main Office';

title: Revenue per top-level category
prompt: Return each top-level category Name (Bikes, Clothing, ...) and its total revenue (sum of SalesOrderDetail.LineTotal), highest revenue first.
hint: Products belong to subcategories. Go up one more level with a self join.

answer.default:
SELECT parent.Name AS Category, SUM(d.LineTotal) AS Revenue
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail d
JOIN SalesLT.Product p ON p.ProductID = d.ProductID
JOIN SalesLT.ProductCategory c ON c.ProductCategoryID = p.ProductCategoryID
JOIN SalesLT.ProductCategory parent ON parent.ProductCategoryID = c.ParentProductCategoryID
GROUP BY parent.Name
ORDER BY Revenue DESC;

title: LEFT JOIN + COUNT
prompt: Return every category's Name and its number of products, including categories with 0 products.
hint: COUNT(*) counts the NULL row too. COUNT(column) skips NULLs.

answer.default:
SELECT c.Name, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS Products
FROM SalesLT.ProductCategory c
LEFT JOIN SalesLT.Product p ON p.ProductCategoryID = c.ProductCategoryID
GROUP BY c.ProductCategoryID, c.Name;

title: Compare to an aggregate
prompt: Return ProductID, Name and ListPrice of products priced above the average ListPrice.

title: IN (subquery)
prompt: Return ProductID and Name of products that appear in at least one order.

title: NOT EXISTS
prompt: Return ProductID and Name of products that have never been ordered.
hint: Be careful with NOT IN: it returns no rows if the subquery contains a NULL.

title: Correlated subquery
prompt: Return ProductCategoryID, Name and ListPrice of the most expensive product(s) in each category (a product whose price equals its category's maximum).
hint: The inner query refers to the outer row (p.ProductCategoryID).

title: Scalar subquery in SELECT
prompt: Return SalesOrderID, TotalDue and the order's share of all orders' TotalDue as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals (TotalDue * 100 / grand total).

title: Derived table
prompt: Return the average number of lines per order as a decimal (one number).
hint: On SQL Server, AVG of an integer column returns an integer. Multiply by 1.0 first. A derived table needs an alias.

title: Simple CTE
prompt: Using a CTE, compute each customer's total spend (sum of TotalDue across their orders). Return CompanyName and TotalSpent for customers who spent more than 50000.

answer.default:
WITH spend AS (
  SELECT CustomerID, SUM(TotalDue) AS TotalSpent
  FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderHeader
  GROUP BY CustomerID
)
SELECT c.CompanyName, s.TotalSpent
FROM spend s
JOIN SalesLT.Customer c ON c.CustomerID = s.CustomerID
WHERE s.TotalSpent > 50000;

title: Recursive CTE: category tree
prompt: Use a recursive CTE to list every category with its Level (1 = top-level, 2 = subcategory) and its Path, e.g. 'Bikes > Road Bikes' (top-level categories have just their name). Return Name, Level, Path.
hint: MySQL and Postgres need WITH RECURSIVE. The string column must have the same type in both halves, so CAST it.

answer.sqlserver:
WITH tree AS (
  SELECT ProductCategoryID, Name, 1 AS Level, CAST(Name AS NVARCHAR(200)) AS Path
  FROM SalesLT.ProductCategory
  WHERE ParentProductCategoryID IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.ProductCategoryID, c.Name, t.Level + 1, CAST(t.Path + ' > ' + c.Name AS NVARCHAR(200))
  FROM SalesLT.ProductCategory c
  JOIN tree t ON c.ParentProductCategoryID = t.ProductCategoryID
)
SELECT Name, Level, Path FROM tree;
answer.mysql:
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
  SELECT ProductCategoryID, Name, 1 AS Level, CAST(Name AS CHAR(200)) AS Path
  FROM SalesLT.ProductCategory
  WHERE ParentProductCategoryID IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.ProductCategoryID, c.Name, t.Level + 1, CONCAT(t.Path, ' > ', c.Name)
  FROM SalesLT.ProductCategory c
  JOIN tree t ON c.ParentProductCategoryID = t.ProductCategoryID
)
SELECT Name, Level, Path FROM tree;
answer.postgres:
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
  SELECT ProductCategoryID, Name, 1 AS Level, CAST(Name AS VARCHAR(200)) AS Path
  FROM SalesLT.ProductCategory
  WHERE ParentProductCategoryID IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.ProductCategoryID, c.Name, t.Level + 1, CAST(t.Path || ' > ' || c.Name AS VARCHAR(200))
  FROM SalesLT.ProductCategory c
  JOIN tree t ON c.ParentProductCategoryID = t.ProductCategoryID
)
SELECT Name, Level, Path FROM tree;

title: Two CTEs
prompt: Using CTEs, compute the revenue (sum of LineTotal) of each subcategory, then return the Name and Revenue of subcategories whose revenue is above the average subcategory revenue.

answer.default:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT c.Name, SUM(d.LineTotal) AS Revenue
  FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail d
  JOIN SalesLT.Product p ON p.ProductID = d.ProductID
  JOIN SalesLT.ProductCategory c ON c.ProductCategoryID = p.ProductCategoryID
  GROUP BY c.Name
),
avg_rev AS (
  SELECT AVG(Revenue) AS AvgRevenue FROM rev
)
SELECT r.Name, r.Revenue
FROM rev r, avg_rev a
WHERE r.Revenue > a.AvgRevenue;

title: ROW_NUMBER per group
prompt: Number the products within each category from most to least expensive (ties broken by ProductID). Return ProductCategoryID, Name, ListPrice, RowNum.

title: Top N per group
prompt: Return the 2 most expensive products of each category (ties broken by ProductID): ProductCategoryID, Name, ListPrice.
hint: You can't use a window function in WHERE. Compute it in a subquery or CTE first.

answer.default:
SELECT ProductCategoryID, Name, ListPrice
FROM (
  SELECT ProductCategoryID, Name, ListPrice,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ProductCategoryID ORDER BY ListPrice DESC, ProductID) AS rn
  FROM SalesLT.Product
) t
WHERE rn <= 2;

title: RANK
prompt: Rank orders by TotalDue, highest = 1. Return SalesOrderID, TotalDue, SalesRank.

answer.default:
SELECT SalesOrderID, TotalDue, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY TotalDue DESC) AS SalesRank
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderHeader;

title: Running total
prompt: For order 71780, return SalesOrderDetailID, LineTotal and a running total of LineTotal ordered by SalesOrderDetailID.

answer.default:
SELECT SalesOrderDetailID, LineTotal,
       SUM(LineTotal) OVER (ORDER BY SalesOrderDetailID) AS RunningTotal
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail
WHERE SalesOrderID = 71780;

title: LAG
prompt: Sorting orders by SalesOrderID, return SalesOrderID, TotalDue and the previous order's TotalDue (NULL for the first order).

answer.default:
SELECT SalesOrderID, TotalDue, LAG(TotalDue) OVER (ORDER BY SalesOrderID) AS PrevTotalDue
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderHeader;

title: Window aggregate
prompt: Return ProductID, Name, ListPrice and the average ListPrice of the product's category (as an extra column, without collapsing the rows).

title: String functions
prompt: Return each product's ProductNumber, the part of ProductNumber before the first '-' as Prefix, and the product Name in upper case.
hint: SQL Server: LEFT + CHARINDEX. MySQL: SUBSTRING_INDEX. Postgres: SPLIT_PART.

answer.sqlserver:
SELECT ProductNumber,
       LEFT(ProductNumber, CHARINDEX('-', ProductNumber) - 1) AS Prefix,
       UPPER(Name) AS UpperName
FROM SalesLT.Product;
answer.mysql:
SELECT ProductNumber,
       SUBSTRING_INDEX(ProductNumber, '-', 1) AS Prefix,
       UPPER(Name) AS UpperName
FROM SalesLT.Product;
answer.postgres:
SELECT ProductNumber,
       SPLIT_PART(ProductNumber, '-', 1) AS Prefix,
       UPPER(Name) AS UpperName
FROM SalesLT.Product;

title: String length
prompt: Return LastName and its length (number of characters) for customers whose LastName is longer than 10 characters.
hint: SQL Server: LEN. MySQL: CHAR_LENGTH (LENGTH counts bytes). Postgres: LENGTH.

title: Date parts
prompt: Return the year products started selling (from SellStartDate) and how many products started that year.
hint: SQL Server and MySQL have YEAR(). Postgres uses EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ...), which also works in MySQL.

title: Date difference
prompt: For products that have a SellEndDate, return Name and the number of days between SellStartDate and SellEndDate as DaysOnSale.
hint: SQL Server: DATEDIFF(day, start, end). MySQL: DATEDIFF(end, start). Postgres: subtract two dates.

title: CASE expression
prompt: Return Name, ListPrice and a PriceBand column: 'Budget' when ListPrice < 100, 'Mid' when under 1000, otherwise 'Premium'.

answer.default:
SELECT Name, ListPrice,
       CASE WHEN ListPrice < 100 THEN 'Budget'
            WHEN ListPrice < 1000 THEN 'Mid'
            ELSE 'Premium' END AS PriceBand
FROM SalesLT.Product;

title: Conditional aggregation
prompt: For each non-NULL Color return Color, the number of products priced 1000 or more (PremiumCount) and the number priced below 1000 (OtherCount).

answer.default:
SELECT Color,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ListPrice >= 1000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS PremiumCount,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ListPrice < 1000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS OtherCount
FROM SalesLT.Product
WHERE Color IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY Color;

title: COALESCE
prompt: Return Name and Color for every product, showing 'N/A' instead of NULL colors.
hint: COALESCE works everywhere. SQL Server also has ISNULL, MySQL has IFNULL.

answer.default:
SELECT Name, COALESCE(Color, 'N/A') AS Color
FROM SalesLT.Product;

title: Aggregate strings
prompt: For each order with fewer than 10 lines, return SalesOrderID and a comma+space separated list of its product names in alphabetical order (e.g. 'A, B, C').
hint: SQL Server: STRING_AGG ... WITHIN GROUP. MySQL: GROUP_CONCAT. Postgres: STRING_AGG(x, sep ORDER BY ...).

answer.sqlserver:
SELECT d.SalesOrderID, STRING_AGG(p.Name, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY p.Name) AS Products
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail d
JOIN SalesLT.Product p ON p.ProductID = d.ProductID
GROUP BY d.SalesOrderID
HAVING COUNT(*) < 10;
answer.mysql:
SELECT d.SalesOrderID, GROUP_CONCAT(p.Name ORDER BY p.Name SEPARATOR ', ') AS Products
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail d
JOIN SalesLT.Product p ON p.ProductID = d.ProductID
GROUP BY d.SalesOrderID
HAVING COUNT(*) < 10;
answer.postgres:
SELECT d.SalesOrderID, STRING_AGG(p.Name, ', ' ORDER BY p.Name) AS Products
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail d
JOIN SalesLT.Product p ON p.ProductID = d.ProductID
GROUP BY d.SalesOrderID
HAVING COUNT(*) < 10;

title: Insert, then use the new id
prompt: Add an address (AddressLine1 '1 Practice Way', City 'Seattle', StateProvince 'Washington', CountryRegion 'United States', PostalCode '98101') and link it to customer 29485 in CustomerAddress with AddressType 'Shipping'. You need the AddressID that was just generated.
hint: SQL Server: SCOPE_IDENTITY() (or OUTPUT INSERTED.AddressID). MySQL: LAST_INSERT_ID(). Postgres: RETURNING, here inside a CTE (or lastval()).

WITH new_address AS (
  INSERT INTO SalesLT.Address (AddressLine1, City, StateProvince, CountryRegion, PostalCode)

title: Update with a JOIN
prompt: Set Comment = 'Bike shop' on every order whose customer's CompanyName contains 'bike' (any letter case). Use a join between SalesOrderHeader and Customer.
hint: Each database writes this differently. SQL Server: UPDATE alias ... FROM ... JOIN. MySQL: UPDATE t JOIN ... SET. Postgres: UPDATE t SET ... FROM other WHERE ...

answer.sqlserver:
UPDATE h
SET Comment = 'Bike shop'
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderHeader h
JOIN SalesLT.Customer c ON c.CustomerID = h.CustomerID
WHERE c.CompanyName LIKE '%bike%';
answer.mysql:
UPDATE SalesLT.SalesOrderHeader h
JOIN SalesLT.Customer c ON c.CustomerID = h.CustomerID
SET h.Comment = 'Bike shop'
WHERE c.CompanyName LIKE '%bike%';
answer.postgres:
UPDATE SalesLT.SalesOrderHeader h
SET Comment = 'Bike shop'
FROM SalesLT.Customer c
WHERE c.CustomerID = h.CustomerID
  AND c.CompanyName ILIKE '%bike%';

title: Update with CASE
prompt: In a single UPDATE, raise ListPrice by 5% for products under 100, by 3% for products from 100 up to (not including) 1000, and leave products at 1000 or more unchanged.

    WHEN ListPrice < 100 THEN ListPrice * 1.05
    WHEN ListPrice < 1000 THEN ListPrice * 1.03

title: Delete with a JOIN
prompt: Delete the order lines (SalesOrderDetail) whose product is in the 'Road Frames' category. Use a join.
hint: SQL Server and MySQL: DELETE alias FROM ... JOIN. Postgres: DELETE FROM t USING other WHERE ...

answer.sqlserver:
DELETE d
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail d
JOIN SalesLT.Product p ON p.ProductID = d.ProductID
JOIN SalesLT.ProductCategory c ON c.ProductCategoryID = p.ProductCategoryID
WHERE c.Name = 'Road Frames';
answer.mysql:
DELETE d
FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail d
JOIN SalesLT.Product p ON p.ProductID = d.ProductID
JOIN SalesLT.ProductCategory c ON c.ProductCategoryID = p.ProductCategoryID
WHERE c.Name = 'Road Frames';
answer.postgres:
DELETE FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail d
USING SalesLT.Product p, SalesLT.ProductCategory c
WHERE p.ProductID = d.ProductID
  AND c.ProductCategoryID = p.ProductCategoryID
  AND c.Name = 'Road Frames';

title: Foreign keys: delete in the right order
prompt: Delete customer 29485 (Catherine Abel) completely. Deleting only the Customer row fails because her order and her address links reference it. Delete the referencing rows first, then the customer. (SalesOrderDetail rows are removed automatically with ON DELETE CASCADE from SalesOrderHeader.)
hint: Try DELETE FROM SalesLT.Customer WHERE CustomerID = 29485 first and read the error. Several statements separated by ; run in one go.

check.default:
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesLT.Customer WHERE CustomerID = 29485) AS Customers,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderHeader WHERE CustomerID = 29485) AS Orders,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesLT.SalesOrderDetail WHERE SalesOrderID = 71782) AS OrderLines,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesLT.CustomerAddress WHERE CustomerID = 29485) AS AddressLinks,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SalesLT.Customer) AS AllCustomers;
